title: GitHub Copilot Pro
catchSummary: Completions are unlimited on paid plans, but chat, agents, and code review draw a $15/mo AI-credit pool — premium models drain it fast, and unused credits are forfeited at month end.

price.now: $10/user/mo (monthly billing; annual price for Pro not published)
price.renewal: Monthly per-user charge. No auto-renew terms page was found in this pass — the docs describe cancellation and proration but not renewal notice, so treat renewal mechanics as unverified.

renewal: Billed monthly per user. Canceling keeps access until the end of the current billing cycle with no proration; upgrades prorate immediately, downgrades take effect next cycle. A personal plan is automatically canceled (with prorated refund) if a company seat overlaps it. Whether the price is locked between renewals: not published.
eligibility: Any individual GitHub account with a supported payment method ($10/user/mo)
Free alternative exists: Copilot Free (2,000 completions + 50 chat requests/mo) and a Student plan for verified students at $0
Teachers and maintainers of popular open-source projects: docs state access at no cost (eligibility mechanics beyond 'verified' not published)
Additional-credit purchase is unavailable for iOS/Android in-app subscriptions per the plans table
restrictions: AI credits (plain-English: monthly usage dollars converted to points — 1 credit = $0.01) gate chat, agent mode, code review, cloud agent, CLI, and Apps; code completions and next-edit suggestions do not use credits and stay unlimited on paid plans
Pro carries $15/mo total credits = $10 base (1,000) + $5 flex (500); unused credits do not carry over — reset 00:00 UTC on the 1st of each month

Premium models (e.g. Claude Opus/Fable, GPT-5.5/5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra) are listed as Pro+/Max access in the docs tier table — Pro's own roster covers Sonnet 4.6/Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.4/5.6 Luna/Terra, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Grok 4.5/4.6, Kimi K2.7/K3, MAI-Code
Continuing past included credits requires setting a dollar budget; GitHub notes additional usage 'may be capped'
Code review also bills GitHub Actions minutes
verdict: At $10/mo Copilot Pro is the cheapest tracked coding-tool subscription, and completions-only users effectively get unlimited service — the credit pool only matters if you lean on chat, agents, or premium models. Roughly $0.15 of metered usage is included daily on a 30-day month; a few Opus-class agent sessions can consume the pool, which is why the budget-and-alert mechanism exists. If your workflow is completion-first, Pro is strong value; if it is agent-first, budget for on-demand spend or price Pro+ ($39, $70/mo credits) alongside it.
catches: The $10 sticker price buys $10 of base credits + $5 flex — not unlimited premium usage; chat/agent/model calls meter against it
Credits reset monthly with no rollover: a light January does not subsidize a heavy February
The plans page's static model table looks identical across tiers — the docs comparison table, not the marketing page, is the reliable tier mapping
Overage requires an explicitly set budget ('budgets do not stop license charges') and may still be capped mid-cycle
limits: Included usage: $15/mo total credits on Pro (1,500 credits at $0.01)
Completions: unlimited on paid plans; Free is 2,000 completions + 50 chats/mo
Premium-model access: excluded at Pro tier per docs table; model options may vary by feature
Per-model token rates (what actually drains credits) live in the models-and-pricing reference, not the plans page
Exact daily caps beyond credits: not published
access_route: Subscribe from the Copilot plans page with a personal GitHub account, install the extension in VS Code/JetBrains, then check Settings → Copilot → Usage for your credit budget and alerts.

claim_steps.step: Open the plans comparison and confirm the Pro column's credit figures ($15 total = $10 base + $5 flex) before subscribing.
Check the docs tier table for which models are on Pro vs. locked to Pro+/Max — do not rely on the marketing card.
After subscribing, set a personal usage budget early; email alerts fire at 75/90/100% of it.
If you are a student, test the free Student plan before paying — verified students get Copilot at no cost.

economics_heading: What $10 actually buys: credits vs. completions
economics: Split the value: completions and next-edit suggestions are unmetered, so completion-only users get the full plan for $10 and never touch the credit pool.

Everything metered (chat, agents, review, CLI) draws credits at per-token model rates; $15/mo of credits is $0.50/day of model calls — one long Opus-class agent session can approach the whole base pool, which is why Pro's roster stops below the premium models.

Break-even framing against the $0.80/task illustrative reference: $10/mo covers roughly 12 metered tasks before on-demand is cheaper-or-dearer parity; below ~12 tasks/mo of chat/agent work, a budget-only setup on Free + occasional usage may cost less — but Free caps chats at 50/mo, so heavy users cross to Pro quickly.
Overage is opt-in: with no budget set you stop at the pool; with a budget you pay $0.01/credit in arrears. Model the pool as a ceiling you must consciously lift, not a soft cap.

evidence.point: Pro $10/user/mo and the $15/$10+$5 credit split were read live on the official plans comparison page (2026-09-07), and the dollar and credit framings agree across plans page, billing docs, and usage-based-billing docs.

No-rollover, monthly reset at 00:00 UTC, budget mechanics (alerts at 75/90/100%, 'budgets do not stop license charges'), and possible capping of additional usage are stated in the official usage-based-billing doc.

Tier-to-model mapping (premium models gated to Pro+/Max) comes from the docs plans table; the features page static table renders an identical roster across tiers, so the docs version is authoritative here.

faq.q: What does GitHub Copilot Pro cost as of the Sep 2026 snapshot?
faq.a: $10/user/mo, billed monthly. The plans page and billing docs both state it; no annual Pro price is published. Prices verified live 2026-09-07 — re-check before paying.

faq.q: What are AI credits and how many does Pro include?
faq.a: Credits are GitHub's metered usage unit at $0.01 each. Pro includes $15/mo total: a $10 base allotment (1,000 credits) plus a $5 flex allotment (500). Completions don't use credits; chat, agents, code review, cloud agents, CLI, and Apps do. Unused credits are forfeited at the monthly reset.

faq.q: What happens when Pro credits run out?
faq.a: Officially you can wait for the next cycle, switch to cheaper models, or set a dollar budget for additional usage billed in arrears at per-token model rates. GitHub notes additional usage may be capped, and budgets do not stop license charges.

faq.q: Can I use frontier premium models on Pro?
faq.a: Not according to the docs tier table, which lists Opus/Fable-class and GPT-5.5/5.6-Sol-class models under Pro+ and Max. Pro's own roster still includes Claude Sonnet 4.6/Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.4/5.6 Terra/Luna, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Grok 4.5/4.6, and Kimi K3. Model options may vary by feature.

Yes — Copilot Free (2,000 completions + 50 chat requests/mo, no credit card) and a Student plan at no cost for verified students; teachers and popular-OSS maintainers are also stated free. The Student plan is auto-model-selection only and excludes third-party agents.
A live pass on 2026-09-07 across the plans page and three docs articles. Billing mechanics change often — re-verify at official docs before relying on budget behavior.
